Quarter-turn ball valves for potable water, hydronic heating, steam, gas and compressed air, in 1/2" through 2" and larger.

Connections stocked include FIP x FIP, press x press, sweat x sweat and the PEX standards F1960 and F1807, so the valve can be joined the same way as the run it sits in. Body material runs brass, bronze, lead-free forged brass and no-lead brass; anything installed on potable water must be lead-free, which is a legal requirement rather than a preference.

Pressure ratings run 150 to 600 WOG. Read the dual marking carefully — a valve stamped 150 WSP / 600 WOG is rated 600 psi for water, oil and gas at ambient temperature but only 150 psi on saturated steam. Full-port and standard-port versions both appear here; full port passes the same bore as the pipe and is what to use where pressure drop matters or where the line will be rodded.

Brands include Apollo-Conbraco, Jomar, Legend Valve and Milwaukee Valve.

Ball valves with press ends, so the valve goes into the line the same way the fittings do — no solder, no thread, no draining the system dry.

Sizes 1/2" through 4", in brass, lead-free brass and bronze, with press x press, press and press x hose connections. Pressure ratings run 200 and 250 WOG depending on body and size.

Two things to check before ordering. The press profile must match your jaws, exactly as it does on the fittings. And on potable water, the body must be lead-free — NSF/ANSI 372 compliance is a marking on the valve, not an assumption you can make from the alloy name.

Full-port versus standard-port matters on a supply line: standard port restricts flow at the valve, which is fine on isolation duty and costly on a main.

A water heater is the appliance most likely to flood a house, and the one most often installed where nobody looks. These are automatic shut-off valves that sit on the cold supply to the heater and close it when a sensor finds water on the floor or in the pan. Orders ship from Seattle, WA.

Taco LEAKBREAKER is a control unit with a motorized 3/4 in. NPT ball valve, actuator and floor sensor, built specifically for a water heater. It is resettable and testable after a trip, so a nuisance alarm does not mean a service call, and it signals with a two-color LED and an audible alarm. The LB-075-H-1LF ships with one sensor, the LB-075-H-2LF with two, for a heater with both a pan and a nearby floor drain. The eLink version (LBW-075-H-2LF) adds WiFi and reports status and trips to your phone.

FloodStop 20001 is the same idea at a lower price point: a 3/4 in. NPT MIP x FIP valve with control unit and sensor. The MIP x FIP body threads inline with the existing supply nipple, so the install is a union break rather than a pipe cut.

Sizing and placement. All four are 3/4 in. NPT, which is the supply on effectively every residential tank heater. Put the valve on the cold inlet, upstream of the heater, and the sensor at the low point of the pan or the floor. A shut-off on the heater protects the heater only — if you want the whole house covered, a main-line valve is the right device.

70 water pressure regulators and service parts, 1/2" through 2": Resideo DS05 and DS06 DialSet (32, including six repair parts), Watts 009 series (13), Cash Acme EB45 and F95 (10), Zurn Wilkins 600XL, 70XL and NR3XL (8), Caleffi North America PressCal (6) and one Apollo-Conbraco direct acting valve. The trade calls the device a PRV and the fixture aisle calls it a water pressure regulator; they are the same valve.

A pressure reducing valve and a pressure relief valve do opposite jobs. A regulator sits on the incoming service and holds downstream pressure at a set point continuously, whether or not anything is wrong. A relief valve does nothing at all until pressure or temperature crosses a limit, then opens and discharges. One is a control, the other is a safety device, and neither substitutes for the other — a building that needs a regulator generally needs both.

Most plumbing codes call for a regulator wherever static supply pressure at the building exceeds 80 psi. Past that point pressure stops being free performance and starts being wear: it is what splits supply lines, cuts fill valve seals and turns a dripping faucet into a replaced cartridge. Measure the street pressure with a gauge before choosing a set point rather than working from the neighborhood's reputation.

Installing a regulator closes the system, and a closed system needs somewhere for hot water to expand. Before the regulator, thermal expansion from the water heater pushed back out into the street main. After it, the regulator blocks that path, pressure climbs against nothing every time the burner fires, and the heater's T&P valve begins to weep — which reads as a failed T&P valve and is not one. The answer is a correctly sized thermal expansion tank put in at the same time, not a second T&P valve.

Adjustment range is a specification, not a preference. The standard range here is 25–75 psi and covers nearly every residential service. Low range valves adjust 10–35 psi and are stocked in 1/2" and 3/4" for services that have to land below what the standard valve will hold. Winding a 25–75 psi valve down to its bottom stop is not the same thing as fitting a low range valve.

Single union against double union is a serviceability decision rather than a hydraulic one. A single union valve is solid on one end, so replacing it later means cutting pipe. A double union breaks loose at both ends and the next valve goes in without touching the piping. On a service entrance buried behind finished wall, the double union is the cheaper part measured across the life of the building.

Ends cover the whole range — female NPT, solder union, press, PEX-A cold expansion and push-to-connect. The connection is a separate choice from the valve. The Resideo DS05, the DS06 DialSet and the Cash Acme EB45 are each stocked in several end configurations of one valve body, so choose the body for the pressure job and the ends for the pipe you are joining. Where Watts states the seat, it tracks size: polymer seat in 1/2" through 1", stainless steel seat in 1-1/4" through 2". The six Caleffi PressCal valves are listed to ASSE 1003 and carry an integral pressure gauge, in NPT and in press, 3/4" through 1-1/4".

Rebuild before replacing. Six of the 70 are service parts rather than valves: Resideo union kits for the DS06 and FK06 in 3/4", 1" and 1-1/2" NPT plus 3/4" sweat, a low lead replacement filter bowl with O-ring for the 1-1/2" and 2", and a union seal washer for the 1". A regulator that will not hold its setting is often a fouled strainer or a cut seal rather than a failed body — the DS06 carries its strainer in a replaceable bowl for that reason.

60 backflow prevention devices from Watts, Zurn Wilkins, Apollo-Conbraco, Arrowhead Brass, Caleffi North America, Cash Acme, Aalberts Integrated Piping and Moen. Assemblies run 1/4" through 3"; air gap fittings cover 1/2" through 6". Most of the range is lead free bronze or lead free brass.

The device class is set by the hazard, not by the pipe size. A reduced pressure principle assembly — the RP, or RPZ where it is built as a reduced pressure zone assembly — is what a high hazard connection needs: it has a relief port that dumps to atmosphere the moment either check fouls, so a failure is visible on the floor instead of silent in the potable line. A double check assembly is a low hazard device and fails closed without telling anyone. A pressure vacuum breaker (PVB) protects against back-siphonage only, not back-pressure, which is why it belongs on irrigation and not on a boiler fill. Substituting down a class because it fits the budget is the one substitution that is never a field call.

On a lawn irrigation or sprinkler system the local code decides between a PVB and an RPZ backflow preventer, and the answer usually turns on whether fertilizer or chemical is injected downstream. A hose bib backflow preventer — a hose connection vacuum breaker threaded onto the sillcock — is the cheapest protection in the building and the one most often missing; eight are stocked here, four of them Watts in 3/4". A residential service entrance is typically a dual check, stocked from 1/4" through 1".

27 of the 60 are testable assemblies. Every reduced pressure, reduced pressure zone and double check assembly here carries test cocks, and in most jurisdictions has to be certified by a licensed tester at installation and then annually. That annual obligation follows the building, so specifying a testable assembly where the code does not require one commits the owner to a recurring cost.

Where the manufacturer publishes limits, the devices are rated 175 psi maximum working pressure and 180°F maximum temperature. ASSE 1013 covers reduced pressure principle assemblies and ASSE 1015 covers double checks; the number on the tag is what the inspector reads.

Rebuilding beats replacing on these. Eight Zurn Wilkins backflow preventer repair kits cover the 375, 375XL, 950XL, 975XL and 975XL2 from 1/4" through 2" — rubber and spring kits for an annual test failure, complete internals when the seats are cut. Match the kit to the model number on the tag, not to the pipe size.

The range breaks down as: reduced pressure principle (RP) assemblies (14), hose connection vacuum breakers (8), repair kits and internals (8), reduced pressure zone (RPZ) assemblies (7), double check valve assemblies (6), dual check valves (6), atmospheric and anti-siphon vacuum breakers (5), air gap fittings (4), pressure vacuum breaker (1), and a 2" Cash Acme EB45-U.

Swing, spring and dual check valves for potable water, hydronic heating and pump discharge, in 1/2" through 2" and larger.

Orientation is the specification people get wrong. A swing check relies on gravity and flow to close its disc, so it only works reliably in a horizontal run or a vertical run with upward flow — installed backwards or on a downflow line, it will not seat. A spring check closes against a spring and works in any orientation, which is why it is the right choice on pump discharge and in tight mechanical rooms.

Spring checks have a higher cracking pressure and therefore a higher pressure drop. On a gravity or low-head system that difference is enough to matter; on a pumped line it usually is not.

Bodies are bronze, brass, lead-free brass and cast iron, in FIP, sweat and press. Ratings run 200 to 300 WOG.

Body HTML:
Shower and tub diverter valves, in-wall rough-in bodies and diverter trims, mostly 1/2" inlet.

A diverter sends water from one outlet to another — tub spout to showerhead, or between multiple shower outlets. A transfer valve is the related but different device: it can feed two outlets at once, which is what a body-spray and rain-head combination needs. Choosing a diverter where a transfer valve was intended means only one outlet ever runs.

Count outlets before ordering. Three-way and six-way diverters exist, and the number is fixed by the valve body in the wall, not by the trim on the face of it. Adding an outlet later means opening the wall.

Rough-in body and finish trim are ordered separately on most manufacturers' systems, which is what lets the valve go in during construction and the finish be chosen at the end. They must be from the same family — trim is not cross-compatible between brands or between generations.

Brands include Moen (M-CORE transfer valves and Posi-Temp with diverter), Grohe, hansgrohe, Delta, Brizo, American Standard, Pfister, TOTO and DXV, with 2-way, 3-way and 3-or-6-function diverter and transfer valve roughs.

The mixing valve that feeds the diverter is in shower and tub-shower valves; the finish trim is in shower trim sets and thermostatic valve trims.

Popular in this collection: Pfister 015-6WDS 4-Port 6-Way Diverter Valve, American Standard Flash 2-Way/3-Way Shared Diverter, Moen U362CIS M-CORE Mixing Valve with Transfer Valve, Moen U361CI M-CORE Transfer Valve.

Frequently asked questions

What does a shower diverter valve do?

A shower diverter valve sends water from the mixing valve to one outlet or another, such as the showerhead, a hand shower or a tub spout. The mixing valve sets the temperature; the diverter only chooses where the water goes.

What is a 3-way diverter valve?

A 3-way diverter has three outlet positions, so it can switch between three outlets, for example a showerhead, a hand shower and body sprays. Some 3-way diverters also have shared positions that run two outlets at once; check the product page.

Can I use a different brand of trim on my diverter valve?

No. The trim has to be made for the rough-in valve in the wall, so match the brand and model of the valve body. The rough-in and the trim are sold separately.

Diverter valve vs transfer valve: what is the difference?

A diverter valve sends all the water to one outlet at a time, such as the tub spout or the showerhead. A transfer valve can also run two outlets together, for example a rain head and body sprays. If you want two outlets on at the same time, choose a transfer valve or a diverter with shared positions.

2-way or 3-way diverter: which do I need?

Count the outlets. A 2-way diverter switches between two outlets, such as a showerhead and a hand shower. A 3-way diverter handles three, such as a showerhead, a hand shower and body sprays. The number is set by the rough-in body in the wall, so plan every outlet before the wall is closed.

How do I pick the right diverter valve?

Start with the brand and family of your mixing valve and trim, because trim only fits its own rough-in. Then match the number of outlets, the inlet connection (sweat, IPS or PEX) and the inlet size, which is 1/2" on most models here. The matching finish pieces are in diverter valve trims.

Ninety-two angle stops and straight stops - the small shut off valve under every sink and toilet - from BrassCraft (38), Legend Valve (28), Dahl Valve (19), LSP Products (4), Grohe (2) and BK Products (1). By body: 44 angle, 22 straight and 22 dual-outlet or tee, plus 4 kits and service stops.

Angle or straight is decided by the wall, not by preference

An angle stop turns the flow 90 degrees, so it is what you use when the supply pipe comes out of the wall and the fixture is above it. A straight stop passes flow in line, for when the pipe comes up out of the floor. That is the whole distinction, and it is the single most common ordering mistake on this category - the valve is otherwise identical inside. Look at the stub-out before you buy, not at the fixture.

The inlet is the decision. The outlet almost never is

Nearly every one of these ends in 3/8" or 1/4" compression on the fixture side, because that is what a supply line expects. The inlet is where the choice lives, and it has to match the pipe already in the wall:

  • Compression - 43 of them, for copper stub-outs
  • FIP - 17, threaded onto a male adapter or nipple
  • F1960 expansion PEX - 11, cold-expansion PEX-a
  • F1807 crimp PEX - 5, copper crimp ring PEX-b
  • Push-fit - 8, including Legend's Insta-Loc II
  • Press - 3 LegendPress, for a press tool
  • CPVC - 2, solvent weld

If you are on PEX, the inlet has to match your system: see F1960 expansion fittings and F1807 crimp fittings for which one you have.

Quarter-turn versus multi-turn

A quarter-turn stop is a ball valve - a chrome ball with a hole through it, sealed by two PTFE seats. A multi-turn stop is a compression washer on a rising stem. The difference matters after ten years, not on day one: the multi-turn washer hardens, bonds to the seat, and shears off when someone finally tries to close it during a leak. That is why a plumber replacing a faucet replaces the stop too. Twenty-nine of these are explicitly 1/4-turn ball type; the Legend 114-201NL is the one deliberate multi-turn in the range.

A compression ferrule is single-use

The brass ring that seals a compression inlet deforms permanently when you tighten the nut. It has taken the shape of that pipe at that depth. Pull the valve off and reuse the old ferrule and it will weep - not immediately, which is worse. Cut the stub back and start with a new ferrule, or use a push-fit or press inlet where the seal is a captured O-ring rather than a crushed ring.

Push-fit and press inlets

Eight push-fit stops, including Legend's Insta-Loc II (114-903NL, 114-904NL, 114-943NL) and BrassCraft's G2PS and G2QPS series, go on a clean cut stub with no tool at all. Three LegendPress stops (114-903PNL, 114-904PNL, 114-913PNL) take a standard press jaw - see press tools and jaws. Both cost more per valve than compression and both pay for themselves the moment you are working in a cabinet you cannot get two wrenches into.

Dual stops and tees

Twenty-two dual-outlet stops and tees, for one stub-out feeding two things: a toilet plus a bidet seat, a sink plus a reverse-osmosis unit, a dishwasher teed off the hot side. BrassCraft's CR1900DVX and R1700DVX families and Legend's 114-801NL and 114-802NL give two independently controlled outlets, usually 3/8" and 1/4". The BrassCraft CT2-664X P and BK 993-016NL are plain tees with no second valve - cheaper, but you lose the ability to shut one branch without the other.

Loose key stops

The BrassCraft KTSCR19X and SCR19X have no handle. They take a removable key, which is what you want in a rental, a school restroom or anywhere a handle would get turned by someone who should not be turning it. Order the key separately and keep it on the truck.

No-lead is not a marketing line

Legend's "No Lead" and LSP's "Lead Free" markings refer to the federal limit that has applied to every potable-water valve sold in the US since 2014: a weighted average of no more than 0.25 percent lead on wetted surfaces, certified to NSF/ANSI 372. Older rough-brass stops from before that rule are still in millions of houses. If you are replacing one on a potable line, the new one has to be certified.

Related

A stop is half of a pair - the supply lines that thread onto it are on their own page. For what sits at the other end, see toilet tanks, toilet repair parts, centerset faucets and pull-out kitchen faucets, or the full bathroom department.

Water leak detectors and smart water shut-off valves for domestic water: whole-house motorized ball valves, appliance-specific shut-off kits, and WiFi point sensors that also watch for freezing. Brands stocked: Moen, Resideo, Taco Comfort Solutions and FloodStop.

Not sure which of the three you need? Our whole-house water leak detection guide covers valve sizing, where each device installs, what each tier costs and how the sensors are wired.

Whole-house shut-off valves go on the main downstream of the service shutoff and close the entire supply when a sensor trips. The Resideo L5 is an actuator on a lead-free ball valve, shipped with a power adapter, a mounting clip and a 5 ft sensing cable, in 1/2", 3/4", 1" and 1-1/4" NPT. Flo by Moen puts detection and shut-off in one body, in 3/4", 1" and 1-1/4". Size the valve to the line you are cutting into, not to a fixture branch: a 1" main needs a 1" valve or the whole house loses pressure through the device.

Appliance shut-off kits cover the known failure points for a fraction of the price of a whole-house valve. FloodStop builds one kit per appliance: 3/4" NPT MIP x FIP for a water heater, two 3/4" 90-degree valves for a washing machine, 1/4" compression for an ice maker and 3/8" compression for a toilet or dishwasher. Taco's LeakBreaker is water-heater specific, a control unit with valve, actuator and sensor that shuts the supply to the heater, with a two-color LED and an audible alarm. It is re-settable and testable after a trip, and the eLink version reports status over WiFi.

Point sensors raise the alarm but close nothing. The Resideo L1 detects water on its own base or anywhere along its 5 ft sensing cable, runs on WiFi with no hub, sounds a 100 dB alarm and sends an app notification. It also reads temperature and humidity, so it warns before a pipe freezes rather than after it bursts. Battery life runs up to three years, the unit is reusable once wiped dry, and cables daisy-chain to cover up to 500 feet from a single detector.

Related: Sump pumps · Relief valves · Ball valves · Air and water test

Popular in this collection: Resideo CHW3610W1001/U Water Leak Detector with Cable Sensor, First Alert VWS01Y-3/4 L5 Wi-Fi Shut-Off Valve.

Frequently asked questions

Whole-house shut-off or appliance shut-off?

A whole-house valve installs on the main water line and can shut off the entire home when any sensor detects a leak. An appliance shut-off protects one point, such as a water heater, washing machine or ice maker, and costs less to install.

Do water leak detectors need Wi-Fi?

Wi-Fi models send alerts to your phone and can close a valve remotely. Battery-only detectors sound a local alarm, which helps only if someone is home to hear it.

What size shut-off valve do I need?

Match the size of the main water line where the valve will be installed. Valves are offered from 1/2 in to 1-1/4 in NPT.

Body HTML:
Flo by Moen puts leak detection and automatic shut-off in one body plumbed into the main, plus battery puck detectors for the fixtures the main valve cannot see. Orders ship from Seattle, WA.

Smart Water Shutoff valves install on the main downstream of the service shutoff. The unit monitors flow, pressure and temperature, runs a nightly pressure test on the plumbing, and closes the supply on its own when it reads a leak. Size the valve to the pipe you are cutting into, not to a fixture branch: a 1 in. main needs the 1 in. unit or the whole house loses pressure through the device. Available in 0.75 in. (900-001), 1 in. (900-006) and 1.25 in. (900-002).

Smart Water Detectors are battery pucks that watch one spot and report to the same app as the valve. Put one in a water heater pan, under a sink base, behind a laundry box or at a sump. They sense water, temperature and humidity, so they warn before a pipe freezes rather than after it bursts. Sold singly (920-004) or in a three-pack (920-005) for a house with several risk points.

Cable and accessories. The 6 ft Smart Leak Detect sensing cable (920-006) extends a puck along a run of pipe or the length of a pan, where a single point would miss the water. The 25 ft extension cable (920-003) reaches an outlet further from the main than the stock lead allows.

Pairing note: the shutoff valve and the detectors work independently, but on the same account the detectors can trigger the valve to close. A whole-house valve without detectors still catches a leak downstream of itself by flow signature; detectors without a valve raise the alarm but close nothing.

Milwaukee Valve is a valve manufacturer, not to be confused with Milwaukee Tool, the power tool brand. Milwaukee Valve makes bronze, brass and cast iron valves for plumbing, hydronic heating and mechanical piping systems.

The House Supplier carries more than 100 Milwaukee Valve items, including:

  • Ball valves: BA-100, BA-400 and BA-475B threaded (FIP) valves, BA-150, BA-450 and BA-485B sweat valves, UPBA-480B and BA-480B press valves, and hose end versions.
  • Gate valves: 105, 1151 and 1182 bronze FIP gate valves and 2885-M flanged cast iron OS&Y gate valves.
  • Check valves: 507, 509 and 510 bronze swing checks, 548T and 1548T spring checks, 1509 and 1510 sweat checks, 2974-M flanged swing checks and 1403, 1404, 1406 and 1425 cast iron wafer checks.
  • Globe and butterfly valves: 502 and 590T bronze globe valves, BB2-100 bronze butterfly valves and CL223E lug style cast iron butterfly valves.

How to choose: match the end connection (FIP, sweat, press or flange) to your piping, and confirm the WOG or SWP pressure rating listed on each product page. Our valve reference guide compares ball, gate, globe and check valves.
